title: Filter in place
hints: `s[:0]` is a slice of length 0 that shares `s`'s backing array and has its full capacity. Appending to it writes over `s` from the front without allocating.
Loop over `s` with `range` and `append` only the elements you keep to `out := s[:0]`. Writing never overtakes reading, so you never overwrite an element you haven't looked at yet.
After the loop, `clear(s[len(out):])` zeroes the leftovers (`s` still has its original length). Then `return out`. An even number satisfies `v%2 == 0` (also true for negatives).
